title: Continuous coefficients and inverses of regular-module endomorphisms
statement: For a scheme X and a topological commutative ring O in Type 0, let R be the abelian sheaf underlying U↦C(U,O). A global continuous function b defines a regular R-module endomorphism by multiplying each section by the pullback of b. An arbitrary regular endomorphism g acts on a section a over U by a times the pullback of its global coefficient, namely its value on 1 over X. Coefficients determine endomorphisms and turn composition into multiplication. A nowhere-zero coefficient makes g monic when O is a domain, and makes g an isomorphism when O is a topological field with continuous inversion away from zero.

source.place: Section 6.8, Definition 6.8.10 and Proposition 6.8.11(1): integral coefficient framework and kernel-closure application; the displayed continuous-function pivot argument is an agent reduction, not a matrix argument written out in Lemma 6.8.7

proof.text: Construct multiplication sectionwise, check addition and naturality directly, and check module linearity on pure tensors. The sheaf tensor comparison reduces the latter equality to associativity in O.

Use the proved section-linearity identity for regular endomorphisms. Naturality along the unique U→X identifies g_U(1) with the restriction of g_X(1); hence g_U(a)=a·g_X(1)|U. This proves coefficient injectivity, the coefficient of a multiplier, and the product formula for composition.

A nowhere-zero coefficient cancels pointwise, so each component is injective; reflect monomorphisms through the sheaf and module forgetful functors. For a field, construct the actual continuous reciprocal b(x)=g_X(1)(x)⁻¹ and its multiplier. The product formula and coefficient injectivity prove both inverse identities, also when X is empty.
